story.head: Special teams lean toward the Panthers
paras: The Panthers (9-5-2) beat Chicago 5-3 on Wednesday, while the Capitals (8-6-0) lost 6-5 to Dallas on Tuesday. Going in, the Panthers are fifth in the Atlantic (tied for 11th in the NHL) and the Capitals fourth in the Metropolitan (tied for 21st).

The Panthers forecheck harder than anyone (1st), hit a lot (1st) and kill penalties well (1st). As for the Capitals, they have had some of the best goaltending in the league (4th), but give up a lot of dangerous shots (27th). They also get the league’s best looks (1st), so the Capitals wait for good looks, but the Panthers settle for hopeful ones. The Cats’ power play (3rd) could do real damage against the Capitals’ penalty kill (25th).

Matthew Tkachuk (4 G / 18 A / 22 P in 16 GP) leads the Panthers in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Sam Reinhart (9 G / 7 A / 16 P in 16 GP) has a team-high nine goals, with eight points in his last five games and six goals in nine games against Washington since 2023-24. For the Capitals, Jordan Kyrou (5 G / 9 A / 14 P in 14 GP) leads the way in scoring, with eight points in his last five games. Alex Tuch (10 G / 2 A / 12 P in 14 GP) has a team-high ten goals, tied for tenth in the NHL, with a point in five straight games against Florida.
Jacob Markström (4-2-1 / .885 SV% in 8 GS) is expected to start for Florida, and Logan Thompson (5-4-0 / .887 SV% in 10 GS) for Washington.
At home, Spencer Carbery likes to send Protas, Dubois and Wilson out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against B. Tkachuk, Bennett and M. Tkachuk.
